info.bio:
There is more than one artist named The Gamblers.

1.) The Gamblers were an American surf rock band formed in Los Angeles, California, in 1959. Distinguished by their vocal harmonies and early instrumental surf songs, the Gamblers are one of the first influential musical acts that recorded surf music, a genre popularized initially in Southern California. The group, lead by primary songwriter Derry Weaver, recorded the "Moon Dawg!" single in late 1959

scenes.name: El LSD y sus descontentos
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: Sintetizado mientras se desarrollaba la bomba atómica, el LSD fue con ella el disolvente más potente de la cultura de los sesenta: «la única respuesta a la bomba» (George Andrews). Convertía el existencialismo atómico en un presente eterno sin lenguaje fuera del pensamiento oriental, hacía ridículos la competencia y el materialismo y abría una brecha sin precedentes entre quienes lo tomaban y quienes no. Dylan lo probó en mayo de 1964; un dentista se lo puso en el café a Lennon y Harrison en marzo de 1965. Seguía siendo legal en el otoño de 1965 y ya no lo controlaba Sandoz sino los contrabandistas: Timothy Leary predicaba una revolución de valores y la «Psychedelic Experience», Ken Kesey y los Merry Pranksters hacían Acid Tests caóticos, John Esam distribuía desde el 101 de Cromwell Road y Michael Hollingshead abrió en Londres el World Psychedelic Centre. En los primeros meses de 1966 pasó al centro de la escena y llegó la reacción: redada en el WPC, reportajes del News of the World, del People y de Life (25 de marzo), condena de treinta años a Leary por marihuana (que pidió una moratoria en abril), Sandoz cortó el suministro, el Gavin Report vetó «Eight Miles High» y «Rainy Day Women», Donovan fue el primer pop star detenido (junio) y California y Nevada prohibieron su posesión. Las primeras batallas las ganaron las autoridades, pero el genio ya había salido de la botella.

podcast.title: Conflicting Lineup Claims
podcast.body: The exact lineup of The Gamblers for the "Moon Dog" / "LSD25" single is shrouded in mystery and subject to significant dispute. While the record features two guitarists, bass, drums, and keyboards, as many as 15 people have been credited over the years. Nick Renee claimed the band was originally "Nick and the Gamblers" with himself, Bruce Johnston, Sandy Nelson, Larry Taylor, James Burton, and Richie Polador engineering, with Kim Fowley involved. Kim Fowley, unusually, denied any involvement. Elliot Ingber stated the group consisted of himself, Larry Taylor, Derry Weaver, Howard Hirsch, and Rod Schaefer. Bruce Johnston had no memory of the record. Given Derry Weaver's credit as writer for "Moon Dog" and the existence of his previous band The Moon Dogs, Elliot Ingber's list is considered mostly correct, with Bruce Johnston likely contributing wordless harmonies, leading to a guessed lineup of Derry Weaver, Larry Taylor, Elliot Ingber, Bruce Johnston, and either Rod Schaefer or Sandy Nelson. "I have seen 15 people credited as having been members of the group that recorded the track."

podcast.title: Mystery and Unreliable Accounts
podcast.body: Details about The Gamblers are largely mysterious, pieced together from fragmented and often contradictory recollections from participants. Many individuals involved are known for credit theft, while others were jobbing musicians who, decades later, were unsure if they even played on the record. The host's own book, "California Dreaming," contains errors regarding this single. "Unfortunately everything about the gamblers is shrouded in mystery."
